title: Fractional Multipliers & The Harmonic Invariance Law

concept.heading: The Harmonic Invariance Theorem ($A \times B = \text{Constant}$)
concept.subText: When two quantities multiply to maintain a constant product, any fractional surge in A requires an exact harmonic reduction in B.
concept.formulaLatex: \text{If } A \text{ increases by } +\frac{1}{x} \implies B \text{ MUST decrease by } -\frac{1}{x+1}

cards.title: 🎯 Universal Duals
cards.content: Price × Consumption = Expenditure | Speed × Time = Distance | Efficiency × Days = Total Work

concept.voiceover: Welcome to Part 1. In competitive exams, you cannot afford 90 seconds of algebraic substitution. When two terms multiply to give a constant, any increase of plus one by x in the first term demands an exact decrease of minus one by x plus one in the second.

workedExample.question: The price of crude oil increases by 16.66%. A refinery reduces monthly consumption by 14.28%. What is the net percentage change in total monthly expenditure?
workedExample.voiceover: Look at this repeated PSU question. Price rises by sixteen point six six percent, which is plus one-sixth, meaning multiplier seven-sixths. Consumption drops by fourteen point two eight percent, which is minus one-seventh, meaning six-sevenths. Multiply seven-sixths by six-sevenths and you get exactly one point zero zero. That is zero percent net change in three seconds flat.

practiceDrill.question: If the salary of Person A is 25% more than Person B, by what percentage is the salary of B less than A?
practiceDrill.voiceover: Now it is your turn. If salary of A is twenty-five percent more than B, how much is B less than A? You have ten seconds on the clock!

concept.heading: Kinematics & Work Invariance Transfer
concept.subText: Distance = Speed × Time and Work = Efficiency × Days follow the exact same reciprocal invariant law.
concept.voiceover: In Part 2, we see that Speed times Time equals Distance. If a train drops speed by one-seventh, journey time immediately surges by plus one-sixth. No equations needed.

workedExample.question: Due to dense fog, an express train reduces speed by 14.28% and takes 24 minutes extra to complete its 200 km run. Find its usual travel time.
workedExample.voiceover: Speed drops by one-seventh, so time increases by one-sixth. This one-sixth is given as 24 extra minutes. Therefore, usual time is 6 times 24 equals 144 minutes.

practiceDrill.question: A modernized machine increases daily production efficiency by 33.33%. By what percentage is the time required to complete a batch reduced?
practiceDrill.voiceover: Second drill! Efficiency increases by thirty-three point three three percent. By what percentage does batch completion time drop? 10 seconds!

concept.heading: Successive Scaling & The Asymmetry Trap
concept.subText: Why symmetric +r% and -r% always yields a net loss of -(r/10)^2%, and how 2D dimensional scaling compounds areas.
concept.voiceover: Part 3 reveals the famous asymmetry trap. If a price is hiked by twenty percent and then discounted by twenty percent, you are NOT back at zero; you have suffered a four percent loss.

workedExample.question: Each side of a square plot is increased by 25%. What is the percentage increase in its total surface area?
workedExample.voiceover: Side increases by twenty-five percent, multiplier five-fourths. Area depends on side squared, so five-fourths squared is twenty-five sixteenths. That gives plus nine sixteenths or fifty-six point two five percent.

practiceDrill.question: An online retail store offers two successive discounts of 20% and 10%. What is the single equivalent overall discount percentage?
practiceDrill.voiceover: Final drill! Two successive discounts of 20% and 10%. What is the single net equivalent discount? You have 10 seconds!
